entries.name: Ajv
entries.use_for: Fastest JSON Schema validator for Node.js and browsers
entries.why: The reference JSON Schema validator in JS; used across OpenAPI and config tooling
entries.summary: Ajv is a JSON Schema validator for Node.js and browsers supporting drafts 06/07/2019-09/2020-12 (draft-04 via ajv-draft-04) and JSON Type Definition (RFC8927). It supports remote and recursive references, OpenAPI keywords like discriminator and nullable, all-errors mode, removing additional properties, defaults, type coercion and i18n error messages.
entries.best_for: Validating JSON data against standard JSON Schema or JTD in JavaScript/TypeScript services, APIs and config loaders where speed and standards compliance matter.
entries.not_for: Defining schemas with a TypeScript-first fluent API (Zod-style). Formats need the ajv-formats plugin, and Node versions below 18 are not supported.

entries.name: ArkType
entries.use_for: TypeScript's 1:1 validator with syntax that mirrors TS types
entries.why: Very fast runtime validation with type-level parsing; supports Standard Schema
entries.summary: ArkType is a TypeScript runtime validation library that parses optimized validators from familiar, type-safe syntax. It is used to check external data such as JSON payloads or forms at the boundaries of your code, similar to Zod. MIT licensed; full documentation is on arktype.io.
entries.best_for: TypeScript projects that want validators written in TypeScript-like syntax with static type inference and runtime checking.
entries.not_for: Plain JavaScript projects or teams needing standard JSON Schema interoperability; the README is minimal, so features beyond basic validation should be checked in the docs.

entries.name: AutoForm
entries.use_for: Render complete React forms automatically from an existing Zod or other schema.
entries.why: Generates forms from schemas with shadcn/ui and other UI adapters, saving boilerplate for admin and CRUD forms.
entries.summary: AutoForm automatically renders forms from an existing data schema, such as a Zod schema via @autoform/zod. It maps schema fields to input components, connects them to your form library and sets up validation, with fieldConfig options and escape hatches for customization. An optional AI coding-assistant skill is provided.
entries.best_for: Quickly generating internal tools, admin panels and simple forms from schemas you already have.
entries.not_for: Complex, highly customized forms: the README says it does not aim to be a full-featured form builder or support every schema edge case.

entries.name: class-validator
entries.use_for: Decorator-based validation for TypeScript classes
entries.why: The validation layer used by NestJS DTOs
entries.stable_reason: Feature-complete decorator validation library; stable API that NestJS relies on
entries.summary: class-validator validates objects using decorators (or non-decorator schemas) on TypeScript class properties, internally using validator.js. You annotate a class with decorators like IsEmail or Length, call validate or validateOrReject, and get an array of ValidationError objects including nested errors. Options include whitelisting and groups; works in browser and Node.js.
entries.best_for: TypeScript backends using classes and decorators (e.g. DTO validation) that want declarative property validation.
entries.not_for: Codebases avoiding classes/decorators or wanting schema-first type inference. Disabling forbidUnknownValues lets unknown objects pass validation, per the README warning.

entries.name: Conform
entries.use_for: Build forms that work without JavaScript and validate on server and client.
entries.why: Designed for Remix/Next.js server actions; progressive enhancement with Zod or Valibot schemas.
entries.summary: Conform is a React form library that progressively enhances HTML forms using web standards. It offers schema-based type safety with Standard Schema support and enhanced Zod and Valibot integration, native Server Actions support for Remix and Next.js, accessibility features, nested objects/arrays and intent buttons. MIT licensed.
entries.best_for: Server-first React apps (Remix, Next.js Server Actions) that want forms that work without JavaScript and validate with Zod or Valibot.
entries.not_for: Non-React frameworks, or purely client-side forms where a client-state form library may fit better.

entries.name: Flutter Form Builder
entries.use_for: Build forms with validation and many ready input fields in Flutter.
entries.why: The most used Flutter form package, reducing boilerplate for field state, validation and value collection.
entries.summary: flutter_form_builder is a Flutter package that removes boilerplate for building forms, validating fields, reacting to changes and collecting user input. It includes ready-made FormBuilder input fields so you do not have to write each FormBuilderField yourself, and supports dynamic and conditional forms.
entries.best_for: Flutter apps with data-entry forms that need validation and easy value retrieval.
entries.not_for: Non-Flutter projects. The roadmap mainly lists solving open issues, so expect maintenance rather than major new features.

entries.name: Formik
entries.use_for: Build forms in React without tears
entries.why: One of the most used React form libraries; common in existing codebases
entries.stable_reason: Mature, feature-complete React form library in maintenance mode; API unchanged for years and still widely downloaded
entries.summary: Formik is a React library for building forms. The GitHub README is minimal and points to formik.org for documentation; it is Apache 2.0 licensed and maintained as a yarn monorepo.
entries.best_for: React codebases already using Formik, or teams wanting a well-known form-state library with broad community examples.
entries.not_for: Non-React projects. The README gives almost no feature detail, so check formik.org for current status and API before choosing it for new work.

entries.name: Joi
entries.use_for: Powerful schema description language and data validator for JavaScript
entries.why: The classic Node.js validation library, widely used for API input validation
entries.summary: joi is a schema description language and data validator for JavaScript, installed via npm install joi. You describe the shape of data with a schema and validate values against it; documentation, API reference and version status are on joi.dev.
entries.best_for: Validating request payloads, configuration and other data in Node.js/JavaScript services with a schema API.
entries.not_for: TypeScript-first projects wanting static type inference from schemas, or standard JSON Schema interoperability; the README itself is only a pointer to joi.dev.

entries.name: Pydantic
entries.use_for: Validate and parse data in Python using type hints.
entries.why: The standard Python validation library (Rust core), used by FastAPI and most LLM tooling.
entries.summary: Python data validation library driven by type hints. You declare models as classes with annotated fields (BaseModel) and Pydantic validates and coerces input data against them. V2 is a ground-up rewrite and still ships V1 as pydantic.v1 for incremental upgrades.
entries.best_for: Validating and parsing request bodies, config, or external data in Python 3.10+ code using standard type annotations, with IDE and linter support.
entries.not_for: Non-Python stacks or browser form handling. V2 has breaking changes from V1, so older codebases need a migration path (the bundled pydantic.v1 helps).

entries.name: React Hook Form
entries.use_for: Manage React form state and validation with minimal re-renders.
entries.why: The most used React form library; uncontrolled inputs keep it fast and resolvers plug in Zod, Yup or Valibot.
entries.summary: React form library built on hooks and uncontrolled inputs, so typing causes few re-renders. Embraces native HTML validation and offers resolvers for Yup, Zod, AJV, Superstruct, Joi and others. Small with no dependencies.
entries.best_for: React or React Native apps needing performant forms with schema validation (Zod/Yup/Valibot) and easy integration with UI component libraries.
entries.not_for: Not for non-React frameworks (Vue, Svelte, Angular) or generating forms from a JSON schema; heavily controlled-input patterns need Controller wrappers.

entries.name: react-jsonschema-form
entries.use_for: Generate React forms from JSON Schema with themes for MUI, Ant, Chakra and more
entries.why: Standard way to render forms from JSON Schema; many UI themes
entries.summary: React component that builds and customizes web forms declaratively from a JSON Schema. Split into packages for utils and several validators (AJV8, cfworker), with theme packages and a live playground.
entries.best_for: Schema-driven forms where the form structure comes from JSON Schema, e.g. admin UIs, config editors, and dynamic forms generated from backend schemas.
entries.not_for: Not for hand-designed, highly custom form layouts or non-React stacks; heavy-weight compared to hook-based form libraries for simple forms.

entries.name: Superforms
entries.use_for: Handle forms with server and client validation in SvelteKit.
entries.why: The de facto SvelteKit form library, supporting many validators and progressive enhancement.
entries.summary: SvelteKit form library with server- and client-side validation via many validator libraries (Zod, Valibot, Yup, Joi, TypeBox, ArkType, VineJS, etc.). Merges PageData and ActionData, focuses invalid fields, detects tainted forms, and supports progressive enhancement.
entries.best_for: SvelteKit apps needing typed forms with form actions, server validation and progressive enhancement, with your choice of validator.
entries.not_for: SvelteKit only; not for React/Vue or other meta-frameworks.

entries.name: TanStack Form
entries.use_for: Build fully type-safe forms in React, Vue, Solid, Angular or Lit.
entries.why: Headless, deeply typed form state with standard-schema validation and adapters for many frameworks.
entries.summary: Headless, framework-agnostic form state library with full TypeScript typing. Provides reactive hooks, sync and async validation with debouncing, nested fields, and adapters for React, Vue, Solid, Angular and Lit.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting deeply typed, headless forms that work across multiple frameworks with custom UI and complex validation workflows.
entries.not_for: Ships no UI components or prebuilt layouts; more setup than simpler form libraries if you only need basic forms in one framework.

entries.name: TypeBox
entries.use_for: JSON Schema type builder with static TypeScript type resolution
entries.why: Generates standard JSON Schema with TS types; used by Fastify and Elysia
entries.summary: Runtime type system that builds in-memory JSON Schema objects while statically resolving matching TypeScript types. Schemas are standard JSON Schema, so they work with validators and OpenAPI tooling.
entries.best_for: Fastify/Elysia-style APIs or anywhere you need JSON Schema as the single source of truth for both TypeScript types and runtime validation.
entries.not_for: Not for teams wanting a Zod-style chained parse/transform API; targets JSON Schema semantics rather than coercion-heavy form parsing.

entries.name: Valibot
entries.use_for: Validate data with a modular, tree-shakable schema library when bundle size matters.
entries.why: Zod-like type safety with a functional API that tree-shakes down to a few hundred bytes.
entries.summary: Modular schema validation library with static TypeScript type inference and a functional API that tree-shakes well. Validates data on servers, in forms and in config files, with zero dependencies and many transformation/validation actions.
entries.best_for: Frontends or edge/serverless code where bundle size matters, and you want Zod-like typing with a pipe-based API.
entries.not_for: Smaller ecosystem and fewer integrations than Zod; functional pipe style may feel unfamiliar if you prefer chained methods.

entries.name: validator
entries.use_for: Go struct and field validation via tags
entries.why: The de facto Go validation library, used by Gin and many APIs
entries.summary: Go package that validates structs and fields using struct tags. Supports cross-field and cross-struct validation, slice/array/map diving, custom validators and translatable error messages.
entries.best_for: Go APIs (e.g. with Gin) that need declarative request-struct validation with minimal boilerplate.
entries.not_for: Go only; tag-based rules live in strings and are checked at runtime, not compile time; not a schema/JSON Schema validator.

entries.name: VeeValidate
entries.use_for: Form validation for Vue with Zod/Yup/Valibot schema support
entries.why: The leading Vue form library with composition API and schema integrations
entries.stable_reason: Mature v4 Vue form library with a settled API; releases are infrequent because it is feature-complete
entries.summary: Vue form validation library with composition API support. Offers declarative field- and form-level, sync and async validation, UI-agnostic components, and integrates with schema libraries such as Zod, Yup and Valibot.
entries.best_for: Vue 3 apps needing flexible validation that works with native inputs or any UI library.
entries.not_for: Vue only; it handles validation and state rather than providing form UI.

entries.name: Vest
entries.use_for: Write form validation as test-like suites, independent of UI framework.
entries.why: Unit-test-style syntax for complex, async and conditional validation that stays readable.
entries.summary: Form validation framework where rules are written like unit-test suites, independent of UI framework. Runs only tests for the changed field, remembers prior results, and discards stale async results.
entries.best_for: Complex, conditional or async validation logic that should stay readable and be shared across frameworks or server and client.
entries.not_for: Not a form state manager or UI binding; you pair it with your own form handling. Test-style syntax is less compact than schema libraries for simple shapes.

entries.name: Yup
entries.use_for: Schema builder for runtime value parsing and validation
entries.why: Long-time default schema validator for Formik and many React form setups
entries.summary: Schema builder for runtime parsing and validation. Define schemas, transform values, and assert shapes, with TypeScript type inference and built-in async validation.
entries.best_for: Existing Formik/React forms or projects already using Yup, and cases needing expressive interdependent validation plus value transformation.
entries.not_for: Newer projects often prefer Zod or Valibot for stricter TypeScript inference; not a form state library.

entries.name: Zod
entries.use_for: Validate data at runtime with schemas that also give you static TypeScript types.
entries.why: The most adopted TS schema library; integrates with tRPC, react-hook-form, AI SDKs and many frameworks.
entries.summary: TypeScript-first schema validation library with static type inference. Define a schema, parse untrusted data, and get typed results. Zero dependencies, about 2kb core, works in Node and browsers, includes JSON Schema conversion.
entries.best_for: TypeScript apps validating API input, env vars, forms or LLM outputs, especially alongside tRPC, react-hook-form and AI SDKs.
entries.not_for: Larger bundle than modular alternatives like Valibot; not intended as a form state manager or for non-JS stacks.
